scenario: 目录用 Easy/Medium/Hard 给 30 道拆解分级；13 道 Hard 常见的是 Uber、YouTube、Payment System，Easy 只有 Bitly、Dropbox 这类题。
scenario_en: The catalog ranks 30 breakdowns as Easy, Medium, or Hard; Hard includes Uber, YouTube, and Payment System, while Easy includes Bitly and Dropbox.
q: Hard 题相比 Easy 题，通常在技术判断上多出的核心难点是什么？
q_en: Compared with Easy problems, what extra technical judgment usually makes a Hard problem harder?
options: 需要额外权衡强一致性、地理/实时约束或多组件间的协同
只是实现代码量更多，核心存储模型和一致性要求不变
只是暴露的接口数量更多，处理逻辑和 Easy 题基本一致
只是题目描述篇幅更长，实际架构模式和 Easy 题相同
why: 难度差距通常不是代码量，而是要多做几层跨组件权衡；Bitly 只判编码，Uber 要同时判地理匹配和实时调度。
why_en: Hard problems are harder mainly because they stack extra cross-component tradeoffs like consistency, geography, or real-time constraints, not because they need more code.
options_en: They add extra tradeoffs like strong consistency, geography, or real-time constraints across components.
They just require more implementation code; the core storage model and consistency requirements stay the same.
They just expose more API endpoints; the request-handling logic is basically the same as an Easy problem.
They just have longer problem descriptions; the actual architecture pattern is the same as an Easy problem.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入后任何后续读取都能立刻看到最新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Strong consistency means any read after a write immediately sees the latest value.

optionExplanations: 对：Hard 题往往要同时权衡一致性、地理和实时这些跨组件约束，这才是难度的真正来源。
错：实现代码量不是难度来源，Hard 题的存储模型和一致性要求本来就比 Easy 题更复杂。
错：接口数量只是表面差异，真正拉开差距的是背后多出的跨组件权衡，处理逻辑并不相同。
错：题目描述篇幅长短和难度无关，Hard 题的架构模式确实比 Easy 题更复杂，不是相同。
optionExplanations_en: Right: Hard problems really do stack judgments like consistency, location, and timing across components — that is the real gap.
Wrong: implementation code volume is not the driver; Hard problems genuinely need a more complex storage and consistency model.
Wrong: endpoint count is surface-level; the real gap is the extra cross-component tradeoffs, and the handling logic is not actually the same.
Wrong: description length has nothing to do with difficulty; the architecture pattern genuinely gets more complex, not identical.

scenario: 同一个系统设计题库里，每道题配一句“它最主要考的技术判断”。判断哪些配对描述准确。
scenario_en: In one system design catalog, each prompt is paired with one line on the main technical judgment it tests. Decide which pairings are accurate.
q: 以下「问题—核心技术判断」配对，哪些正确？（多选）
q_en: Which problem-to-core-judgment pairs are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Bitly——主要考短码生成（保证全局唯一、不冲突）和高读写比下的重定向读路径（缓存）
Dropbox（简化版）——主要考大文件上传（分块、断点续传、直传对象存储）和多设备之间的变更同步
Ticketmaster——主要考短码生成与重定向，没有并发一致性要求
News Aggregator——主要考抓取聚合第三方内容并给高读流量生成 feed，写路径不需要跨实体强一致事务
why: Bitly 的难点是短码唯一和重定向读放大；Dropbox 简化版的难点是大文件上传和多端同步；News Aggregator 是抓取 + 读多写少的 feed。C 把 Bitly 的描述套在 Ticketmaster 上，而 Ticketmaster 真正要处理的是并发抢票：同一个座位不能卖两次，需要预留锁 / 事务。
why_en: Bitly's challenge is unique short codes plus a read-heavy redirect path; simplified Dropbox's is large-file upload and multi-device sync; News Aggregator is crawling plus a read-heavy feed. C copies Bitly's description onto Ticketmaster, whose real challenge is concurrent ticket sales: one seat must never be sold twice, which needs reservation locks or transactions.
options_en: Bitly — mainly tests short-code generation (globally unique, no collisions) and the read-heavy redirect path (caching).
Dropbox (simplified) — mainly tests large-file upload (chunking, resumable, direct-to-object-storage) and syncing changes across devices.
Ticketmaster — mainly tests short-code generation and redirect, with no concurrency-consistency need.
News Aggregator — mainly tests crawling and aggregating third-party content and serving feeds to heavy read traffic; the write path needs no cross-entity strongly consistent transactions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把长 URL 映射成的一小段可读字符串。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A short code is a compact string mapped to a long URL.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一组必须整体成功或整体失败的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A transaction is a group of operations that must all succeed or all fail together.

optionExplanations: 对：Bitly 的难点是短码全局唯一不冲突，以及高读写比下重定向的读路径（缓存）。
对：Dropbox 简化版主要考大文件分块上传、断点续传、直传对象存储，以及多设备间变更同步。
错：这套“短码+重定向”的描述是套用 Bitly 的，Ticketmaster 真正要处理的是并发抢票下的预留锁与事务。
对：新闻聚合主要是抓取聚合第三方内容并为高读流量生成 feed，写路径不需要跨实体强一致事务。
optionExplanations_en: Right: Bitly's challenge is globally unique short codes plus the read-heavy redirect path (caching).
Right: simplified Dropbox mainly tests chunked, resumable large-file upload straight to object storage, plus multi-device change sync.
Wrong: that redirect description is borrowed from Bitly — Ticketmaster's real challenge is reservation locks and transactions under concurrent ticket sales.
Right: the news aggregator crawls third-party content and serves a read-heavy feed; the write path needs no cross-entity strongly consistent transactions.

scenario: 你是系统设计新手，第一次想独立走完一遍完整的面试流程，还没建立起「需求→判断→方案」的节奏。
scenario_en: You are new to system design and want to walk through a full interview flow before you have the rhythm of requirement to judgment to design.
q: 为什么应该先挑 Bitly 这类 Easy 题，而不是直接上手 ChatGPT、Payment System 这类 Hard 题？
q_en: Why start with an Easy problem like Bitly instead of jumping straight to Hard problems like ChatGPT or Payment System?
options: Hard 题的题面文字更长，仅读题就要花更多时间去理解
Easy 题通常只孤立考一个核心判断，方便先练熟整套流程
Easy 题不需要设计 API 接口和数据模型这些环节
Hard 题只出现在大厂面试里，创业公司完全不会考
why: Easy 题把判断收窄到一个点（如编码/元数据），新手能先练熟节奏，再叠加一致性、实时性等多重判断。
why_en: Easy problems isolate one technical judgment, so a beginner can first master the requirement-to-design flow before stacking on consistency and real-time constraints.
whenOtherWins: 如果你已有丰富的分布式系统经验、目标是资深岗位，直接从 Medium/Hard 切入更省时间。
tradeoff: 先练单一判断的完整流程 vs 直接挑战多重判断的深度
options_en: Hard problems just have noticeably longer prompts that take more time to read and parse.
Easy problems usually isolate one core judgment, so it's easier to first practice the whole flow.
Easy problems don't require designing an API surface or a data model at all.
Hard problems only show up in big-company interviews; startups never ask them.
optionExplanations: 错：题面长短只影响阅读时间，跟要不要先练完整流程没关系。
对：Easy 题只孤立考一个核心判断，新手能先把「需求→判断→方案」的节奏走一遍。
错：Easy 题照样要设计 API 和数据模型，只是判断本身更单一。
错：Hard 题在创业公司面试里也常出现，跟公司规模无关。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: prompt length only affects reading time, unrelated to whether you should drill the full flow first.
Right: Easy problems isolate one core judgment, letting a beginner first run through requirement, judgment, and design.
Wrong: Easy problems still need an API and a data model; only the underlying judgment is simpler.
Wrong: Hard problems show up at startups too, unrelated to company size.

scenario: 目录里的本地配送服务（如几十分钟送达的「最后一公里」配送）和普通电商发货是两类不同的系统。
scenario_en: A local delivery service, such as last-mile delivery within tens of minutes, is different from ordinary e-commerce shipping.
q: 本地配送服务和普通电商发货相比，多出的核心技术判断是什么？
q_en: Compared with ordinary e-commerce shipping, what extra technical judgment does local delivery add?
options: 要为用户上传的视频做多分辨率转码后再分发
要支持多人同时在同一份文档上做实时协同编辑
要按用户位置匹配附近仓点的库存与配送范围
要对用户的股票买卖单做强一致撮合并保证价格优先
why: 本地配送要在几十分钟内送达，每次查询都要按用户位置实时找出能覆盖它的附近仓点，再合并这些仓点的库存和配送范围/时效。普通电商也会挑仓发货，但时效以天计，不需要在查询时做这种实时的“位置 + 库存”联动。
why_en: Local delivery promises arrival within tens of minutes, so every availability query must find the nearby warehouses that cover the user's location and combine their inventory and delivery range in real time. Ordinary e-commerce also picks a warehouse, but with day-level delivery it does not need this real-time location-plus-inventory join on every query.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    User["User location"] --> Match["Match nearby warehouses"]
    Match --> Stock["Check local inventory"]
    Stock --> ETA["Compute delivery ETA"]
options_en: Transcode uploaded video into multiple resolutions before distributing it.
Support multiple users doing real-time collaborative editing on the same document.
Match user location to the inventory and range of nearby warehouses.
Match users' stock buy/sell orders with strong consistency and price priority.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从本地仓点到用户手中的最后一段配送。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The last mile is the final delivery leg from a local warehouse to the customer.

optionExplanations: 错：这是视频平台上传后转码分发的需求，跟配送要不要匹配库存和范围没关系。
错：这是文档协同编辑的实时冲突合并问题，本地配送不涉及多人编辑同一文档。
对：本地配送要按用户位置找到覆盖它的仓点，再看库存和配送范围，这才是多出的判断。
错：这是交易撮合的强一致与价格优先问题，跟配送的地理匹配是两码事。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: that's a video platform's upload-then-transcode need, unrelated to matching inventory and delivery range.
Wrong: that's real-time collaborative-edit conflict merging; local delivery has nothing to do with co-editing a document.
Right: local delivery has to find the warehouse covering the user's location, then check its stock and range.
Wrong: that's trading-match strong consistency and price priority, a different problem from geo-matching for delivery.

scenario: 价格追踪服务（如持续追踪电商商品历史价格、命中目标价就提醒用户的服务）没有官方实时价格推送可用。
scenario_en: A price tracking service watches e-commerce price history and alerts users when a target price is hit, but there is no official real-time price feed.
q: 这类价格追踪服务的核心技术判断是什么？
q_en: What is the core technical judgment for this kind of price tracking service?
options: 订阅一个官方实时价格推送流，从不主动轮询抓取快照
只保存最新一次价格快照，历史价格全部覆盖丢弃
把每次价格写入都当强一致事务处理，保证多副本瞬间同步
主动采集价格快照（如定期抓取），存成时间序列，命中阈值再触发提醒
why: 没有官方推送，价格只能靠自己主动采集：定期爬取是主通道，也可以辅以浏览器插件等用户端上报。要支持历史价格和降价提醒，就要把快照按时间序列存下来，再做阈值比较。
why_en: Without an official push feed, the service has to collect prices itself: scheduled crawling is the main channel, optionally supplemented by client-side reports such as a browser extension. To support history and price-drop alerts, snapshots are stored as a time series and compared against thresholds.
options_en: Subscribe to an official real-time price push feed and never poll for snapshots.
Only keep the latest price snapshot and overwrite/discard all history.
Treat every price write as a strongly consistent transaction synced instantly across replicas.
Actively collect price snapshots (e.g., scheduled crawling), store them as a time series, and fire alerts when a threshold is crossed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按固定周期主动去源头查询最新数据，而不是等对方推送。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Polling means periodically asking a source for the latest data instead of waiting for it to push updates.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按时间顺序记录的一串数据点，用来看历史趋势。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A time series is a sequence of data points ordered by time, used to see trends.

optionExplanations: 错：题目已说明没有官方实时推送可用，这个前提在本题不成立。
错：只存最新快照并覆盖历史，就没法回溯价格趋势，也判断不出降价提醒。
错：强一致事务解决的是并发写冲突，价格快照更需要的是按时间序列存储。
对：没有推送就要自己主动采集（定期抓取为主，也可辅以用户端上报），把快照存成时间序列，命中阈值再提醒。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: the prompt already says there's no official realtime feed, so this assumption doesn't hold here.
Wrong: keeping only the latest snapshot and overwriting history loses the trend needed to detect a price drop.
Wrong: strong-consistency transactions solve write conflicts, not the need to store snapshots as a time series.
Right: with no push feed, collect prices yourself (scheduled crawling as the main channel, optionally client reports), store snapshots as a time series, and alert on threshold hits.

scenario: 这四道题都在同一个题库里，用来对照「问题」和「它真正考的技术判断」。
scenario_en: These four prompts are from the same catalog and are used to match each problem with the technical judgment it really tests.
q: 以下「问题—核心技术判断」配对，哪些正确？（多选）
q_en: Which problem-to-core-judgment pairs are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Ticketmaster——核心判断是并发抢票下的锁与事务串行化
WhatsApp——核心判断是端到端实时消息投递与在线状态
Rate Limiter——核心判断是限流算法与跨节点计数一致性
YouTube——核心判断是并发抢票下的锁与事务串行化
why: Ticketmaster、WhatsApp、Rate Limiter 各自判断不同；YouTube 的真实核心是上传转码与全球分发，不是抢票锁。
why_en: Ticketmaster, WhatsApp, and the rate limiter each test a different judgment, while YouTube's real core is upload, transcoding, and global delivery, not ticket locking.
options_en: Ticketmaster — the core judgment is locking and transaction serialization under concurrent ticket sales.
WhatsApp — the core judgment is end-to-end real-time message delivery and presence.
Rate Limiter — the core judgment is a throttling algorithm with consistent cross-node counting.
YouTube — the core judgment is locking and transaction serialization under concurrent ticket sales.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让并发操作表现得像按某个顺序一个个执行，避免冲突。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Serialization makes concurrent operations behave as if executed one at a time in some order, avoiding conflicts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标记用户当前是否在线、最近活跃时间的状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Presence is the status that shows whether a user is currently online and when they were last active.

termDefinitions.meaning: 限制单位时间内允许通过的请求数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Rate limiting caps how many requests are allowed to pass through in a given time window.

optionExplanations: 对：抢票场景下多人同时抢同一张票，靠锁和事务串行化保证不超卖。
对：即时通讯要做到实时投递，还要维护每个用户的在线状态。
对：限流器要在多节点间保证计数一致，不然限流阈值会被绕过。
错：这段抢票锁描述搬自 Ticketmaster，YouTube 真正的核心是转码流水线和全球分发。
optionExplanations_en: Right: many buyers race for the same ticket, so locking and transaction serialization prevent overselling.
Right: instant messaging needs realtime delivery plus tracking each user's online status.
Right: a rate limiter needs consistent counting across nodes, or the throttle threshold gets bypassed.
Wrong: that locking description is copied from Ticketmaster — YouTube's real core is transcoding and global delivery.

scenario: 这四道题都在同一个题库里，用来对照「问题」和「它真正考的技术判断」。
scenario_en: These four prompts come from the same catalog and compare each problem with the technical judgment it really tests.
q: 以下「问题—核心技术判断」配对，哪些正确？（多选）
q_en: Which problem-to-core-judgment pairs are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Uber——核心判断是海量司机实时位置的地理匹配与调度
Google Docs——核心判断是多用户并发编辑的冲突合并（如 OT/CRDT）
Payment System——核心判断是资金正确性：幂等防重复扣款、持久化记账、与支付网关对账
Yelp——核心判断是多用户并发编辑的冲突合并（如 OT/CRDT）
why: Uber 考实时位置的地理匹配与调度；Google Docs 考并发编辑合并（OT/CRDT）；Payment System 考资金正确性——幂等、持久记账和对账，跨外部支付网关做不到分布式强一致，只能靠这些手段收敛。Yelp 的核心是按位置的邻近搜索，不是协同编辑合并。
why_en: Uber tests geo-matching and dispatch over live locations; Google Docs tests merging concurrent edits (OT/CRDT); Payment System tests money correctness — idempotency, durable ledgers, and reconciliation, since you cannot get distributed strong consistency across an external gateway. Yelp's core is location-based proximity search, not collaborative-edit merging.
options_en: Uber — the core judgment is geo-matching and dispatch over massive real-time driver locations.
Google Docs — the core judgment is merging concurrent multi-user edits (e.g. OT/CRDT).
Payment System — the core judgment is money correctness: idempotency against double charges, durable ledger records, and reconciliation with the payment gateway.
Yelp — the core judgment is merging concurrent multi-user edits (e.g. OT/CRDT).

termDefinitions.meaning: 两种让多人同时编辑同一文档也能合并出一致结果的算法思路。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OT and CRDT are two algorithm families that let multiple people edit the same document and still converge to a consistent result.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一个请求重复执行多次，结果和只执行一次一样。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idempotency means repeating the same request multiple times has the same effect as doing it once.

optionExplanations: 对：Uber 要在海量司机实时位置里做地理匹配，再调度给乘客。
对：多人同时敲同一份文档，得靠 OT/CRDT 这类算法合并冲突。
对：支付不能重复扣款也不能丢账，靠幂等 key、持久化记账和与支付网关的对账来保证。
错：这段冲突合并描述搬自 Google Docs，Yelp 真正的核心是按距离排序的邻近搜索。
optionExplanations_en: Right: Uber has to geo-match massive real-time driver locations, then dispatch to riders.
Right: when many people type in the same doc, conflicts need merging via OT/CRDT-style algorithms.
Right: payments must not double-charge or lose records, which comes from idempotency keys, durable ledger records, and reconciliation with the payment gateway.
Wrong: that conflict-merge description is copied from Google Docs — Yelp's real core is distance-ranked proximity search.

scenario: Dropbox 和 YouTube 都属于「存储与分发文件/媒体」方向，目录把前者标 Easy、后者标 Hard。
scenario_en: Dropbox and YouTube both involve storing and distributing files or media, but the catalog marks Dropbox as Easy and YouTube as Hard.
q: YouTube 比 Dropbox 多出的核心技术判断是什么？
q_en: What core technical judgment does YouTube add beyond Dropbox?
options: 两者的核心判断完全相同，差别只在数据量更大一些
YouTube 完全不需要考虑任何存储成本问题
YouTube 还要做转码与自适应码率流式播放，Dropbox 核心在分块同步与元数据
Dropbox 反而更难，因为它要处理协同编辑冲突合并
why: 两者都要大文件分块上传、对象存储，也都可以用 CDN 加速下载。Dropbox 的核心是分块同步和版本元数据（并发修改按 last-write-wins 处理，不做内容合并）；YouTube 多出一整条转码流水线：切片、转成多种码率/格式、生成 manifest，让播放端按网速自适应切换。
why_en: Both need chunked large-file upload and object storage, and both can use a CDN for downloads. Dropbox's core is chunked sync and version metadata (concurrent edits resolve by last-write-wins, not content merging); YouTube adds a whole transcoding pipeline: segmenting, encoding into multiple bitrates/formats, and producing manifests so players can switch adaptively by bandwidth.
tradeoff: 同步 + 版本元数据（Dropbox） vs 转码 + 全球分发（YouTube）
options_en: Both test exactly the same judgment; only the data volume is a bit larger.
YouTube does not need to consider any storage cost at all.
YouTube adds transcoding and adaptive-bitrate streaming; Dropbox's core is chunked sync and metadata.
Dropbox is actually harder, because it has to handle collaborative-edit conflict merging.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把上传的视频转换成不同分辨率和编码格式，适配不同设备和网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Transcoding converts an uploaded video into different resolutions and codecs to fit various devices and networks.

optionExplanations: 错：两者数据量都大，但核心判断不同，不是“一样只是量大”。
错：YouTube 存储和分发海量视频，存储成本反而是重要考量。
对：两者都要分块上传和对象存储；Dropbox 核心是分块同步与版本元数据，YouTube 多出转码与自适应码率流式播放。
错：Dropbox 的并发修改按 last-write-wins 处理，不做内容合并；协同编辑冲突合并是 Google Docs 的难点。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: both handle large data volumes, but the core judgment differs — it's not just a size difference.
Wrong: YouTube stores and serves massive video, so storage cost is very much a consideration.
Right: both need chunked upload and object storage; Dropbox's core is chunked sync plus version metadata, while YouTube adds transcoding and adaptive-bitrate streaming.
Wrong: Dropbox resolves concurrent edits by last-write-wins without merging content; collaborative-edit merging is Google Docs's challenge.

scenario: FB News Feed 和 Instagram 都属于“feed 流”方向，目录把前者标 Medium、后者标 Hard。两份拆解里 feed 都是“关注关系 fan-out + 按时间倒序”。
scenario_en: FB News Feed and Instagram are both feed-style systems; the catalog marks News Feed as Medium and Instagram as Hard. In both breakdowns the feed is follow-graph fan-out in reverse chronological order.
q: Instagram 比 FB News Feed 多出的核心技术判断是什么？
q_en: What core technical judgment does Instagram add beyond FB News Feed?
options: 两者的核心判断完全相同，区别只在界面风格不同，别无其他
Instagram 要把 feed 换成算法推荐排序，News Feed 不需要
Instagram 不需要处理名人大号的 fan-out 问题，所以 News Feed 更难
Instagram 还要扛照片/视频大文件上传与分发（直传对象存储 + CDN），feed fan-out 判断两者相同
why: 两份拆解的 feed 部分是同一套判断：按关注关系预计算 feed、按时间倒序，名人账号走写时/读时混合 fan-out。Instagram 多出来的是媒体：手机原图/视频体积大，要用 presigned URL 直传对象存储、生成多尺寸，再经 CDN 全球分发——这就是它比 News Feed 高一档的原因。B 与题面“按时间倒序”矛盾；C 错在 Instagram 拆解恰恰专门处理了名人 fan-out。
why_en: The feed part of both breakdowns is the same judgment: precomputed follow-graph feeds in reverse chronological order, with hybrid fan-out for celebrity accounts. What Instagram adds is media: large photos/videos uploaded directly to object storage via presigned URLs, resized into variants, and served globally through a CDN — which is why it sits one tier higher. B contradicts the stated reverse-chronological feed; C is wrong because the Instagram breakdown explicitly handles celebrity fan-out.
tradeoff: 关系图 fan-out 排序（News Feed） vs 媒体存储 + 独立发现排序（Instagram）
options_en: Both test exactly the same judgment; the only difference is visual style, nothing else.
Instagram must switch the feed to algorithmic ranking, while News Feed does not.
Instagram never has to deal with celebrity fan-out, so News Feed is harder.
Instagram additionally handles large photo/video upload and delivery (direct-to-object-storage + CDN); the feed fan-out judgment is the same.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一条内容主动推送/写入到所有关注者的 feed 里的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out is the process of pushing or writing one piece of content into every follower's feed.

optionExplanations: 错：两者的 feed 部分相同，但 Instagram 多出媒体上传与分发，不是只有界面风格不同。
错：两份拆解的 feed 都按时间倒序，Instagram 并没有换成算法推荐排序。
错：Instagram 拆解恰恰专门处理了名人大号的 fan-out，这一点两题相同。
对：feed 的 fan-out 判断两者相同，Instagram 多出的是大文件直传对象存储、多尺寸生成和 CDN 分发。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: the feed part is the same, but Instagram adds media upload and delivery, so it is more than visual style.
Wrong: both breakdowns use a reverse-chronological feed; Instagram does not switch to algorithmic ranking.
Wrong: the Instagram breakdown explicitly handles celebrity fan-out, the same as News Feed.
Right: the feed fan-out judgment is shared, and what Instagram adds is direct-to-object-storage uploads, multi-size variants, and CDN delivery.

scenario: WhatsApp、FB Live Comments、Google Docs 都要给用户「实时」体验，Bitly 只是一次性跳转，不需要长连接。
scenario_en: WhatsApp, FB Live Comments, and Google Docs need a realtime user experience, while Bitly is a one-shot redirect and does not need persistent connections.
q: 以下哪些是「实时通信/协作」类系统的共同技术要求？（多选）
q_en: Which requirements are common to realtime communication or collaboration systems? Select all that apply.
options: 服务器要能主动推送更新给客户端，而不是让客户端不停轮询
要记录每条长连接落在哪台服务器上（连接/订阅路由），更新才能推到正确的连接
三者都必须为多人同时修改同一份内容提供冲突合并策略
只需要每天批量生成一次汇总报表即可满足需求
why: 三者都靠长连接让服务器主动推送，也都要知道某个用户/观众连在哪台服务器上，否则消息到了别的节点推不出去。冲突合并只属于 Google Docs 这类协同编辑：WhatsApp 消息和直播评论都是追加写，没有“多人改同一份内容”，所以 C 不是共同要求。D 是离线批处理思路。
why_en: All three rely on persistent connections for server push, and all must know which server a user/viewer is connected to, otherwise an update landing on another node can't be delivered. Conflict merging belongs only to collaborative editing like Google Docs: WhatsApp messages and live comments are append-only, with no concurrent edits to the same content, so C is not a shared requirement. D is an offline batch mindset.
options_en: The server must actively push updates to clients instead of clients polling repeatedly.
The system must track which server each persistent connection lives on (connection/subscription routing) so updates reach the right connection.
All three must provide a conflict-merge strategy for multiple people editing the same content at once.
A once-a-day batch summary report is enough to meet the requirement.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端和服务器保持打开的连接，服务器可随时主动推送。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A persistent connection stays open between client and server so the server can push updates at any time.

optionExplanations: 对：轮询有延迟又浪费资源，三者都靠服务器主动推送。
对：要知道每条连接落在哪台服务器上，更新才能路由到正确的连接，否则到了别的节点推不出去。
错：冲突合并只属于 Google Docs 这类协同编辑；WhatsApp 消息和直播评论都是追加写，不是三者共同要求。
错：一天一次的批量报表是离线思路，跟“实时”的要求正好相反。
optionExplanations_en: Right: polling adds delay and wastes resources, so all three rely on server push.
Right: you must know which server each connection lives on so an update can be routed to it, otherwise it lands on another node and cannot be delivered.
Wrong: conflict merging belongs only to collaborative editing like Google Docs; WhatsApp messages and live comments are append-only, so it is not shared by all three.
Wrong: a once-a-day batch report is an offline approach, the opposite of what realtime requires.

scenario: Uber、Yelp、本地配送服务都要回答「附近有什么」；其中 Uber 司机和配送骑手的位置几秒一变，Yelp 商户的位置几乎不变。LeetCode 判题完全不涉及用户地理位置。
scenario_en: Uber, Yelp, and local delivery all need to answer what is nearby; Uber drivers and delivery couriers move every few seconds, while Yelp businesses almost never move. A LeetCode judge does not use the user's physical location.
q: 以下哪些是「地理位置/邻近搜索」类系统的共同技术要求？（多选）
q_en: Which requirements are common to location or proximity-search systems? Select all that apply.
options: 需要按地理范围高效查询（如 geohash/quadtree 这类空间索引）
需要承受位置的高频更新（如坐标每几秒刷新一次）
需要把距离当作排序/匹配的一个因子
核心瓶颈是保存每次查询结果的历史版本
why: 三类系统都靠空间索引做范围查询，并把距离纳入排序或匹配，这是共同点。位置高频更新只属于 Uber 和配送这类移动实体系统；Yelp 商户位置几乎不变，是读多写少，所以 B 不是共同要求。保存查询历史版本与这类系统无关。
why_en: All three rely on spatial indexes for range queries and use distance in ranking or matching — those are shared. High-frequency location updates belong only to moving-entity systems like Uber and delivery; Yelp businesses barely move and the workload is read-heavy, so B is not shared. Storing query-result history is unrelated.
options_en: They need efficient range queries over geography (e.g. geohash/quadtree spatial indexes).
They must absorb high-frequency location updates (e.g. coordinates every few seconds).
They use distance as a ranking or matching factor.
The core bottleneck is storing historical versions of every query result.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把经纬度编码成一段字符串，前缀相同的区域彼此靠近，便于范围查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Geohash encodes latitude and longitude into a string where nearby areas share a common prefix, enabling range queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种把二维空间递归四等分的树结构，用来加速空间范围查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quadtree is a tree that recursively splits 2D space into four quadrants to speed up spatial range queries.

optionExplanations: 对：范围查询要靠 geohash/quadtree 这类空间索引，不然全表扫描太慢。
错：只有移动实体（司机、骑手）才有高频位置写入；Yelp 商户几乎不动，这不是共同要求。
对：不管是打车还是配送，距离都是排序和匹配的关键因子。
错：保留每次查询结果的历史版本不是这类系统的共同瓶颈，范围查询才是。
optionExplanations_en: Right: range queries need spatial indexes like geohash/quadtree, or a full scan gets too slow.
Wrong: only moving entities like drivers and couriers produce high-frequency location writes; Yelp businesses barely move, so this isn't shared.
Right: whether ride-hailing or delivery, distance is a key ranking and matching factor.
Wrong: storing historical versions of query results isn't the shared bottleneck — range queries are.

scenario: Distributed Cache、Job Scheduler、Web Crawler 都是面向后端组件本身的 Hard 题，不是面向终端用户的产品功能。
scenario_en: Distributed Cache, Job Scheduler, and Web Crawler are Hard backend-infrastructure prompts, not end-user product features.
q: 以下「问题—核心难点」配对，哪些正确？（多选）
q_en: Which problem-to-core-challenge pairs are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Distributed Cache——核心难点是分片与副本一致性
Job Scheduler——核心难点是任务队列与 worker 池的调度解耦
Web Crawler——核心难点是抓取前沿队列与去重
三者的核心难点都是前端页面的样式适配
why: 三道基础设施题各自的难点都不同：分片一致性、队列调度、抓取去重；样式适配根本不是这类题的考点。
why_en: Each infrastructure problem has a distinct core challenge — sharding consistency, queue scheduling, and crawl dedupe — none of which is frontend styling.
options_en: Distributed Cache — the core challenge is sharding and replica consistency.
Job Scheduler — the core challenge is decoupling the task queue from the worker pool.
Web Crawler — the core challenge is the crawl frontier queue and deduplication.
All three problems' core challenge is frontend styling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据按某个规则切分到多台机器上存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits data across multiple machines according to some partitioning rule.

termDefinitions.meaning: 爬虫里还没抓取、等待被访问的 URL 队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The crawl frontier is the queue of URLs a crawler has discovered but not yet visited.

optionExplanations: 对：分布式缓存要把数据分片，还得保证副本之间一致。
对：调度器要靠队列把任务和 worker 池解耦，方便独立扩缩容。
对：爬虫要维护待抓取的前沿队列，还得去重避免重复抓取。
错：这三道都是后端基础设施题，压根不考前端样式。
optionExplanations_en: Right: a distributed cache must shard data and also keep replicas consistent.
Right: a scheduler decouples tasks from the worker pool via a queue, so each can scale independently.
Right: a crawler must maintain a frontier queue of URLs to visit and dedupe them.
Wrong: all three are backend infrastructure problems; frontend styling is never the point.

scenario: FB News Feed、FB Live Comments、FB Post Search 都是 Meta 系产品在系统设计面试里的常见原型。
scenario_en: FB News Feed, FB Live Comments, and FB Post Search are common Meta-style product prompts in system design interviews.
q: 以下「问题—核心技术挑战」配对，哪些正确？（多选）
q_en: Which problem-to-core-technical-challenge pairs are correct? Select all that apply.
options: FB News Feed——核心挑战是好友关系的推送分发与排序
FB Live Comments——核心挑战是超高并发下的实时评论流分发
FB Post Search——核心挑战是全文/索引检索，而不是时间线排序
三者的核心挑战都是端到端加密密钥管理
why: News Feed 靠 fan-out 排序，Live Comments 靠高并发实时分发，Post Search 靠全文检索——三者挑战互不相同。
why_en: News Feed relies on fan-out ranking, Live Comments on high-concurrency realtime distribution, and Post Search on full-text indexing — three distinct challenges.
options_en: FB News Feed — the core challenge is friend-graph fan-out and ranking.
FB Live Comments — the core challenge is realtime comment distribution under extreme concurrency.
FB Post Search — the core challenge is full-text/index retrieval, not timeline ranking.
All three problems' core challenge is end-to-end encryption key management.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一条内容主动推送/写入到所有关注者的 feed 里的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out is the process of pushing or writing one piece of content into every follower's feed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对文本内容建立倒排索引，支持按关键词快速查找。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Full-text search builds an inverted index over text content to support fast keyword lookup.

optionExplanations: 对：News Feed 要把内容 fan-out 推给好友，再按权重排序展示。
对：热门直播下评论量瞬间暴涨，分发要扛住超高并发。
对：搜历史帖子靠的是全文索引检索，不是按时间排序。
错：这三道题的核心都不是密钥管理，是各自不同的分发/检索机制。
optionExplanations_en: Right: News Feed fans content out to friends, then ranks it by weight for display.
Right: comments spike instantly under a popular livestream, so distribution must absorb extreme concurrency.
Right: searching past posts relies on full-text indexing, not chronological ordering.
Wrong: none of the three hinge on key management; each has its own distribution or retrieval mechanism.

scenario: 目录里同时有「YouTube」和「YouTube Top K」两道 Hard 题，名字很像但考点完全不同。
scenario_en: The catalog has both YouTube and YouTube Top K as Hard prompts; their names are similar, but the tested skills are different.
q: YouTube Top K 这道题真正考的技术判断是什么？
q_en: What technical judgment does the YouTube Top K prompt actually test?
options: 视频上传后的多分辨率转码流水线设计
全球 CDN 边缘节点的选址与调度策略
海量播放事件流上按时间窗的 Top-K 计数
用户账号的强一致性鉴权与会话管理
why: YouTube Top K 问的是：从海量播放事件流里，按最近 1 小时 / 1 天 / 1 月 / 全量这些时间窗，算出播放最多的 K 个视频。拆解的基线要求是精确结果；用 count-min sketch 等近似结构换性能，是可以和面试官讨论的权衡，不是默认答案。和视频存储转码无关。
why_en: YouTube Top K asks for the K most-viewed videos over windows like the last hour, day, month, and all time, computed from a massive view-event stream. The breakdown's baseline requires precise results; approximate structures like count-min sketch are a trade-off to discuss, not the default. It is unrelated to video storage or transcoding.
options_en: Designing the multi-resolution transcoding pipeline after video upload.
Choosing where and how to schedule global CDN edge nodes.
Windowed top-K counting over a massive view-event stream.
Strongly consistent account authentication and session management.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在海量数据流里出现频率特别高的那一小撮元素。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heavy hitter is one of the small set of elements that appears unusually often in a massive data stream.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种用少量内存近似统计数据流中元素出现频率的数据结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A count-min sketch is a data structure that approximates element frequencies in a data stream using very little memory.

optionExplanations: 错：这是普通 YouTube 题的考点，Top K 版本关注的是统计，不是转码流水线。
错：CDN 选址是分发问题，跟怎么从海量事件里算出热门 K 个视频无关。
对：题目要的是从海量播放事件里按时间窗算出播放最多的 K 个视频，属于流计数范畴，跟存储转码无关。
错：鉴权会话管理是账号安全问题，跟统计最热视频没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: that's the plain YouTube prompt's focus; the Top K version is about counting, not the transcoding pipeline.
Wrong: CDN placement is a delivery problem, unrelated to computing the top K hottest videos from event volume.
Right: it asks for the K most-viewed videos over time windows from a flood of view events, a streaming-count job unrelated to storage or transcoding.
Wrong: auth and session management is an account-security concern, unrelated to ranking the hottest videos.

scenario: ChatGPT 这道 Hard 题和 Web Crawler、Metrics Monitoring 这类经典基础设施 Hard 题归在同一档难度里。
scenario_en: The ChatGPT prompt is ranked Hard alongside classic infrastructure prompts like Web Crawler and Metrics Monitoring.
q: 相比 Web Crawler 这类经典基础设施题，设计 ChatGPT 这类 AI 产品多出的核心技术判断是什么？
q_en: Compared with a classic infrastructure prompt like Web Crawler, what extra technical judgment does a ChatGPT-style AI product add?
options: 要权衡模型推理延迟/吞吐，并管理会话上下文
完全不需要考虑存储和缓存这类基础设施
只是把实现语言换成另一种编程语言
和网络爬虫的技术挑战完全一样，只是名字不同
why: AI 产品多一层模型服务判断：推理延迟/吞吐怎么权衡、怎么流式吐 token、上下文怎么管理，这是传统爬虫题没有的。
why_en: AI product design adds a model-serving layer of judgment — inference latency versus throughput, streaming token generation, and context management — that classic crawling problems don't have.
options_en: You must trade off inference latency versus throughput and manage conversation context.
Storage and caching infrastructure are not a concern at all.
It just swaps in a different implementation language.
It has exactly the same technical challenges as a web crawler, just a different name.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用已经训练好的模型对新输入产出结果的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Inference is the process of running a trained model on new input to produce an output.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型边生成边逐个 token 返回，而不是等全部生成完再一次性返回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Streaming generation returns tokens one at a time as the model produces them, instead of waiting for the full output.

optionExplanations: 对：这类产品比传统爬虫题多算一层推理服务：延迟/吞吐怎么取舍、会话上下文怎么管理。
错：存储和缓存照样要设计，只是在此之上还多了模型服务这一层。
错：换编程语言不改变技术判断，真正加的是模型推理这层新问题。
错：爬虫的核心是抓取去重，AI 产品的核心是推理服务，两者判断完全不同。
optionExplanations_en: Right: these AI products add a whole inference-serving layer, trading off latency against throughput, and tracking session context.
Wrong: storage and caching are still needed; the model-serving layer is added on top, not a replacement.
Wrong: swapping languages doesn't change the technical judgment; the real addition is the inference layer.
Wrong: a crawler's core is fetch-and-dedupe, an AI product's core is inference serving — the judgments are unrelated.

scenario: 你想专项练习「并发争抢同一份有限资源」这类技术判断——锁、事务、串行化。
scenario_en: You want to specifically practice the judgment where many clients contend for the same limited resource: locks, transactions, and serialization.
q: 练并发争抢有限资源时，最适合的两道 Medium 题是？
q_en: When practicing contention over a limited resource, which two Medium problems are the best fit?
options: Ticketmaster 和 Online Auction，两者都是多人抢同一份资源，练锁与事务
Bitly 和 Dropbox，两者是短链重定向和文件同步，不涉及并发抢占同一资源
Strava 和 Tinder，两者靠位置做邻近查询，不是并发写冲突
News Aggregator 和 LeetCode，分别是内容聚合和代码沙箱，也不涉及资源争抢
why: 抢票和拍卖出价都是同一份资源被并发争抢，直接练锁、事务和串行化；其余选项都缺这层并发写冲突。
why_en: Ticket sales and auction bids both have many clients contending for the same limited resource, directly exercising locking, transactions, and serialization.
whenOtherWins: 想在更高难度下练一致性与并发，可进阶到 Hard 的 Robinhood 或 Payment System。
tradeoff: 并发争抢单一资源的锁/事务 vs 其他题型各自的技术判断
options_en: Ticketmaster and Online Auction — both have many people racing to claim the same resource, exercising locks and transactions.
Bitly and Dropbox — short-link redirects and file sync, neither involves contention over one resource.
Strava and Tinder — both do location-based proximity queries, not concurrent write conflicts.
News Aggregator and LeetCode — content aggregation and a code sandbox, also unrelated to resource contention.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个请求同时争夺同一份有限资源（如同一张票）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Contention is when multiple requests compete for the same limited resource at the same time, like one ticket.

optionExplanations: 对：抢票和拍卖出价都是多人抢同一份资源，直接练锁、事务和串行化。
错：短链重定向和文件同步都没有并发争抢同一资源，练不到锁和事务。
错：Strava 和 Tinder 考的是地理邻近查询，不涉及并发写冲突。
错：内容聚合和判题沙箱各自的核心跟并发争抢资源都不沾边。
optionExplanations_en: Right: both ticket sales and auction bids have many people racing for the same resource, exactly what exercises locking and serialization.
Wrong: redirect and file sync never have concurrent contention over one resource, so neither drills locking.
Wrong: Strava and Tinder both test geo-proximity queries, not concurrent write conflicts.
Wrong: content aggregation and the code sandbox each test something unrelated to resource contention.

scenario: Design LeetCode 要在页面里安全地运行任意用户提交的代码，再判断输出是否正确。
scenario_en: Design LeetCode needs to safely run arbitrary user-submitted code and then judge whether the output is correct.
q: Design LeetCode 的核心技术判断是什么？
q_en: What is the core technical judgment in Design LeetCode?
options: 只是一个带语法高亮和自动补全的前端编辑器组件而已
要在隔离沙箱里安全运行不受信任代码，并判定结果
核心其实是对题目内容和历史题解做全文搜索索引
核心其实是对提交的代码文件做转码压缩处理
why: 用户提交的代码不可信，必须在资源受限、网络隔离的沙箱里跑完再收集结果，这是判题系统最核心的安全判断。
why_en: User-submitted code is untrusted, so it must run inside a resource-limited, network-isolated sandbox before results are collected.
options_en: It's just a frontend editor component with syntax highlighting and autocomplete, nothing more.
Untrusted code must run safely inside an isolated sandbox, then be judged.
The core is actually building a full-text search index over problem statements and past solutions.
The core is actually transcoding and compressing the submitted code files.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个资源受限、和外部网络隔离的执行环境，用来安全运行不受信任的代码。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sandbox is a resource-limited, network-isolated execution environment used to safely run untrusted code.

optionExplanations: 错：编辑器只是前端展示，真正的挑战在后端怎么安全跑代码。
对：提交的代码不能信任，得放进限资源、断网络的隔离环境里跑完再判定结果。
错：全文搜索索引是搜索题的考点，判题系统的核心是安全执行，不是搜索。
错：转码压缩是视频/文件类题的考点，跟怎么安全跑用户代码无关。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: the editor is just the frontend; the real challenge is running code safely on the backend.
Right: since the code cannot be trusted, execution has to happen in a resource-capped, network-cut box, then the output gets checked.
Wrong: full-text indexing is a search problem's concern; a judge system's core is safe execution, not search.
Wrong: transcoding and compression belong to video/file problems, unrelated to safely running user code.

scenario: Strava（运动轨迹记录）和 Tinder（附近的人匹配）都要用到用户的地理位置。
scenario_en: Strava records exercise routes and Tinder matches nearby people, so both depend on user location.
q: Strava 和 Tinder 共同的地理位置判断是什么？
q_en: What location-based judgment do Strava and Tinder share?
options: 都要采集用户 GPS 坐标并做地理距离计算（Strava 累计轨迹里程，Tinder 按距离筛候选人）
都需要强一致的资金交易对账
都需要处理用户上传视频的转码与分发
都完全不涉及用户实时位置的更新
why: 两题都以用户 GPS 坐标为输入：Strava 在运动中按固定间隔采样坐标，用 Haversine 公式累计里程、画轨迹；Tinder 用用户位置按距离筛出候选人（这里才需要空间索引做邻近查询）。共同点是“位置采集 + 地理计算”，邻近查询只是 Tinder 的需求。
why_en: Both take the user's GPS coordinates as input: Strava samples coordinates at fixed intervals during an activity and uses the Haversine formula to accumulate distance and draw the route; Tinder uses the user's location to filter candidates by distance (that is where a spatial index for proximity queries comes in). The shared judgment is location capture plus geographic computation; proximity search is Tinder-specific.
options_en: Both collect users' GPS coordinates and compute geographic distance (Strava accumulates route distance; Tinder filters candidates by distance).
Both need strongly consistent financial-transaction reconciliation.
Both need to transcode and distribute user-uploaded videos.
Neither involves updating the user's real-time location at all.
optionExplanations: 对：两者都以用户 GPS 坐标为输入做地理距离计算，Strava 累计轨迹里程，Tinder 按距离筛候选人；邻近查询只是 Tinder 的需求。
错：两者都不涉及资金流转，谈不上金融对账。
错：转码分发是媒体平台的考点，跟运动轨迹和交友匹配没关系。
错：两者都要持续采集用户位置，Strava 靠它记轨迹，Tinder 靠它筛附近的人。
optionExplanations_en: Right: both take GPS coordinates as input and compute geographic distance; Strava accumulates route distance, Tinder filters candidates by distance, and proximity search is Tinder-specific.
Wrong: neither app moves money, so financial reconciliation isn't relevant here.
Wrong: transcoding and delivery are a media platform concern, unrelated to routes or matching people.
Wrong: both keep capturing the user's location; Strava records the route with it and Tinder filters nearby people with it.

scenario: Robinhood（股票交易）和 Payment System（支付系统）都属于金融方向的 Hard 题。
scenario_en: Robinhood, a stock-trading prompt, and Payment System are both Hard financial-system prompts.
q: Robinhood 和 Payment System 共同的金融一致性判断是什么？
q_en: What financial consistency judgment do Robinhood and Payment System share?
options: 都以最终一致性为默认目标，优先换取更高吞吐
都主要考验静态资源的 CDN 缓存策略
关键写路径（扣款、下单、账本记录）要强一致，并用幂等键防重复扣款或重复下单
都不需要处理并发写入
why: 钱和交易不能算错也不能算两次。两道题都要求关键写路径（余额、订单状态、账本）强一致，再用幂等键挡住重试造成的重复。和外部 PSP、交易所的交互通常是异步的，靠对账收敛，所以不是「全链路强一致」。
why_en: Money and trades can't be wrong or counted twice, so both problems need strong consistency on the critical write path (balances, order state, ledger) and idempotency keys to absorb retries. Interactions with external PSPs or exchanges are usually asynchronous and converge through reconciliation, so this is not end-to-end strong consistency.
options_en: Both default to eventual consistency to prioritize higher throughput.
Both are mainly tested on static-asset CDN caching strategy.
The critical write path (charges, orders, ledger entries) needs strong consistency, plus idempotency keys to prevent double charges or duplicate orders.
Neither needs to handle concurrent writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一个请求重复执行多次，结果和只执行一次一样。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idempotency means repeating the same request multiple times has the same effect as doing it once.

optionExplanations: 错：金钱和交易不能算错，两者都不能只满足于最终一致，得要强一致。
错：CDN 缓存解决的是静态资源分发，跟防止重复扣款没关系。
对：资金和订单一旦算错或重复计入代价极大，关键写路径必须靠强一致性和幂等键兜底。
错：两者都有大量并发写，比如同一账户的并发扣款、同一用户的并发下单。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: money and trades can't be wrong, so neither can settle for eventual consistency alone — they need strong consistency.
Wrong: CDN caching solves static-asset delivery, unrelated to preventing duplicate charges.
Right: a wrong or double-counted charge or order is costly, so the critical write path relies on strong consistency plus idempotency keys.
Wrong: both see heavy concurrent writes, such as concurrent debits on one account or concurrent orders from one user.

scenario: Ad Click Aggregator（广告点击聚合）和 Metrics Monitoring（指标监控）都要处理源源不断涌入的海量事件。
scenario_en: Ad Click Aggregator and Metrics Monitoring both handle a continuous high-volume stream of incoming events.
q: Ad Click Aggregator 和 Metrics Monitoring 共同的事件流判断是什么？
q_en: What event-streaming judgment do Ad Click Aggregator and Metrics Monitoring share?
options: 基于地理位置做邻近范围搜索匹配
海量事件流按时间窗做实时聚合（计数/汇总）
多副本间文件版本号的强一致同步
端到端加密的会话密钥分发与轮换
why: 两题都要把源源不断的事件按时间窗实时聚合成统计结果（流处理）。注意 Ad Click 要用于计费，拆解要求不丢点击、结果准确，还会加周期性对账（reconciliation）纠正流处理的偏差，所以这里不能默认“近似统计”。
why_en: Both must aggregate a continuous event stream into windowed statistics in real time (stream processing). Note that ad clicks drive billing: the breakdown requires no lost clicks and accurate results, adding periodic reconciliation to correct the streaming layer, so approximate statistics are not the default here.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Events["High-volume events"] --> Stream["Stream processing"]
    Stream --> Agg["Aggregation"]
    Agg --> Store["Query store / dashboard"]
options_en: Location-based proximity range search and matching.
Real-time windowed aggregation (counts/rollups) over massive event streams.
Strongly consistent syncing of file version numbers across replicas.
End-to-end encrypted session-key distribution and rotation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据一到达就立刻处理，而不是攒成批次再处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Stream processing handles data as soon as it arrives instead of waiting to process it in batches.

optionExplanations: 错：这是地理类题的考点，跟点击/指标事件流的聚合没关系。
对：两边都要把持续涌入的海量事件按时间窗汇总成统计结果，属于流处理方向（广告点击还要求准确并做对账）。
错：文件同步考的是版本一致，跟事件流聚合是两个方向。
错：密钥分发是安全问题，跟统计事件流完全不搭边。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: that is a geo-search concern, unrelated to aggregating click or metric event streams.
Right: both continuously roll incoming events into windowed stats, a streaming-aggregation pattern like Top K (ad clicks additionally need accuracy and reconciliation).
Wrong: file sync is about version consistency, a different direction from event-stream aggregation.
Wrong: key distribution is a security concern, entirely unrelated to aggregating event streams.

scenario: 你的目标公司常考「设计一个聊天/消息系统」，要挑一道有完整拆解的题精练实时消息与在线状态。
scenario_en: Your target company often asks for a chat or messaging system, and you want one full breakdown to practice realtime delivery and presence.
q: 练聊天/消息系统时，最对口的拆解题是哪道？
q_en: When practicing a chat or messaging system, which breakdown is the closest match?
options: News Aggregator
WhatsApp
Price Tracking Service
Job Scheduler
why: WhatsApp 直接覆盖实时消息投递、在线状态这些聊天系统的核心判断，其余三道都是完全不同的技术方向。
why_en: WhatsApp directly covers realtime message delivery and presence, the core judgments of a chat system, while the other problems test unrelated directions.
whenOtherWins: 想练「高扇出的直播评论流」选 FB Live Comments；想练协同编辑选 Google Docs。
tradeoff: 实时消息投递 + 在线状态（WhatsApp） vs 其他题各自的技术方向
options_en: News Aggregator.
WhatsApp.
Price Tracking Service.
Job Scheduler.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标记用户当前是否在线、最近活跃时间的状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Presence is the status that shows whether a user is currently online and when they were last active.

optionExplanations: 错：News Aggregator 练的是抓取聚合，不涉及实时投递或在线状态。
对：它把消息实时投递和在线状态这两项聊天系统的核心判断都覆盖到了。
错：价格追踪练的是轮询和时间序列，跟聊天系统的实时投递不是一回事。
错：任务调度练的是队列和 worker 解耦，跟聊天消息投递无关。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: News Aggregator drills crawling and aggregation, nothing about realtime delivery or presence.
Right: it nails both getting messages there instantly and tracking who is online, the two things a chat system needs.
Wrong: price tracking drills polling and time series, a different problem from realtime chat delivery.
Wrong: job scheduling drills queueing and worker decoupling, unrelated to message delivery.

q: 补全 Hello Interview 目录里四道 Easy 入门系统设计题（填目录原名 / 拆解里用的产品名）：
q_en: Fill in the four Easy starter prompts from the Hello Interview catalog (use the catalog / breakdown product names):
text: 四道 Easy：{{Bitly}}（短链）、{{Dropbox}}（文件同步）、Local Delivery Service（{{Gopuff}}）、News Aggregator（Google News）。
why: 这四道各自把判断收窄到一个孤立的核心技能——编码重定向、版本元数据、地理+库存匹配、内容聚合。
why_en: Each easy problem isolates one core skill — redirect encoding, version metadata, geo-plus-inventory matching, or content aggregation — before stacking on more constraints.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把长网址映射成短字符串的服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A short link service maps a long URL to a short string.

scenario: Online Chess 里两名玩家要实时对弈，任何一步棋都要让对方立刻看到，还要防止非法走子。
scenario_en: In Online Chess, two players play in real time; each move must appear to the other player quickly, and illegal moves must be blocked.
q: Online Chess 的核心技术判断是什么？
q_en: What is the core technical judgment in Online Chess?
options: 对局记录做强一致的批量离线归档就足够了
核心是给棋盘图片做多级 CDN 缓存加速
核心是给用户账号和余额做支付对账
低延迟的走子状态同步，加上服务端合法性校验
why: 两人对弈要求走子几乎实时可见，且不能信任客户端上报的棋步，所以核心是低延迟同步加服务端校验。
why_en: A two-player game needs moves to appear almost instantly and can't trust the client's reported move, so the core is low-latency sync plus server-side legality checks.
options_en: Batch-archiving the game record with strong consistency offline is enough.
The core is multi-tier CDN caching to speed up board images.
The core is payment reconciliation for user accounts and balances.
Low-latency move-state synchronization plus server-side legality validation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务端独立检查一步棋是否符合规则，而不是只信任客户端。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Legality validation means the server independently checks whether a move follows the rules instead of trusting the client.

optionExplanations: 错：对局记录归档是次要的收尾工作，跟走子要不要实时同步没关系。
错：棋盘图片是静态资源，CDN 缓存解决不了走子要不要实时同步的问题。
错：对弈本身不涉及支付，把支付对账搬进来是跑题了。
对：走子要几乎实时可见，还不能信任客户端上报，所以要低延迟同步加服务端校验。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: archiving game records is a secondary wrap-up task, unrelated to whether moves sync in real time.
Wrong: a chessboard image is a static asset — CDN caching doesn't solve realtime move synchronization.
Wrong: a chess match involves no payments, so reconciliation is off-topic here.
Right: moves must appear almost instantly and the client cannot be trusted, so it needs low-latency sync plus server-side validation.

scenario: 游戏排行榜要实时显示 top-N 和某个玩家的名次，百万级玩家分数频繁更新，读榜和查名次都要快。
scenario_en: A game leaderboard must show the top-N and any player's rank in real time; scores change constantly across millions of players, and both listing and rank lookups must be fast.
q: Game Leaderboard 的核心技术判断是什么？
q_en: What is the core technical judgment in a Game Leaderboard?
options: 用按分数排序的结构（ZSET）增量维护名次和 top-N
每次读榜都对关系表按 score 做 ORDER BY 全表排序再分页
给每个玩家分数存独立缓存 key，读时全取回内存里排序
定期离线批量跑全量排序生成静态榜单供查询
why: 排行榜要按分数实时取名次和 top-N，需要一个始终有序、可增量更新的结构（如 Redis ZSET）：更新分数和取名次是 O(log n)，取 top-N 是 O(log n + N)。代价是整个有序集合要放在内存里；规模再大时要按分数段或赛区分片，跨分片算全局名次会变复杂；持久化另靠 RDB/AOF 快照。
why_en: A leaderboard needs live rank and top-N by score, so it uses an always-sorted, incrementally updated structure such as a Redis sorted set: score updates and rank lookups are O(log n), top-N is O(log n + N). The cost is keeping the whole set in memory; at larger scale you shard by score range or region, which makes global rank harder; durability comes separately from RDB/AOF snapshots.
options_en: Maintain rank and top-N incrementally in a score-sorted structure (a sorted set / ZSET).
Re-sort the whole relational table with ORDER BY on score on every read, then paginate.
Store each player's score under its own cache key and sort them all in memory at read time.
Run a periodic offline batch full-sort that produces a static board for reads.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的有序集合，成员按 score 排序，支持 O(log n) 取名次和范围查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sorted set is a Redis structure that keeps members ordered by score and supports O(log n) rank and range queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: SQL 里按某列排序返回结果的子句，全表排序在大表上很昂贵。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ORDER BY is the SQL clause that sorts result rows by a column; sorting a whole large table is expensive.

optionExplanations: 对：排行榜按分数排序，ZSET 让取名次和 top-N 都是 O(log n)，还能增量更新。
错：每次读都全表 ORDER BY 排序，百万玩家下 CPU 顶不住，做不到实时。
错：分数拆成独立 key，读榜要全取回再排序，等于根本没有排序结构。
错：离线批量排序出的榜单是过期快照，显示不了实时名次。
optionExplanations_en: Right: a leaderboard sorts by score, and a sorted set gives O(log n) rank and top-N with incremental updates.
Wrong: full-table ORDER BY on every read melts the CPU at millions of players and can't be real time.
Wrong: splitting scores into separate keys forces you to fetch all and sort at read time — no sorted structure at all.
Wrong: an offline batch-sorted board is a stale snapshot and can't show live rank.

scenario: 通知系统要把一条事件经 push、邮件、短信多渠道发给用户，要尊重免打扰和渠道偏好，且不能重复轰炸。
scenario_en: A notification system must deliver one event to users across push, email, and SMS, respecting do-not-disturb and channel preferences, without spamming duplicates.
q: Notification System 的核心技术判断是什么？
q_en: What is the core technical judgment in a Notification System?
options: 统一异步扇出管线依用户偏好选渠道，配去重和重试
事件发生时同步串行调用每个渠道 provider，任一失败就整体报错
所有通知只走 push 单一渠道以简化投递逻辑
用分布式强一致事务保证每条通知恰好投递一次
why: 一条事件要扇到多渠道并依用户偏好过滤，provider 抖动时要重试，所以核心是异步扇出管线加去重；代价是只能做到至少一次投递，靠幂等键兜住重复。
why_en: One event fans out to several channels by preference and retries on failure, so the core is an async fan-out pipeline with dedup; the cost is at-least-once delivery, deduped by idempotency keys.
options_en: A unified async fan-out pipeline that picks channels by user preference, with dedup and retries.
Synchronously call each channel provider in series when the event fires; any failure fails the whole thing.
Send every notification over a single push channel to simplify delivery.
Use a distributed strongly-consistent transaction to guarantee exactly-once delivery of each notification.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一条消息复制分发到多个下游（渠道或订阅者）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out means duplicating one message out to many downstream targets such as channels or subscribers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用幂等键识别并丢弃重复投递，避免同一通知发多次。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Deduplication uses an idempotency key to detect and drop duplicate deliveries so the same notification isn't sent twice.

termDefinitions.meaning: 至少一次投递：保证不丢，但可能重复，需要下游幂等。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: At-least-once delivery guarantees a message is never lost but may arrive more than once, so consumers must be idempotent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 实际负责投递的第三方服务，如 APNs、SMTP、短信网关。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A provider is the third-party service that actually delivers a message, such as APNs, SMTP, or an SMS gateway.

optionExplanations: 对：多渠道要依用户偏好扇出，还要在 provider 失败时重试，所以要异步管线加去重。
错：同步串行调每个 provider，一个渠道慢或挂就拖垮整条投递。
错：只走 push 会漏掉没开推送的用户，也违背多渠道和偏好需求。
错：跨外部 provider 做不到恰好一次，强上事务只会牺牲可用性。
optionExplanations_en: Right: multi-channel delivery must fan out by user preference and retry on provider failure, so it needs an async pipeline with dedup.
Wrong: calling each provider synchronously in series lets one slow or failing channel stall the whole delivery.
Wrong: push-only misses users who disabled push and ignores the multi-channel and preference requirements.
Wrong: exactly-once across external providers is unattainable; forcing a transaction just sacrifices availability.

scenario: GitHub Actions 每次 push 都要跑用户提供的 CI 脚本（不可信代码），从一个 runner 池调度执行，并限制每个账号的并发。
scenario_en: On every push, GitHub Actions must run user-supplied CI scripts (untrusted code), dispatching them across a pool of runners while capping each account's concurrency.
q: GitHub Actions 的核心技术判断是什么？
q_en: What is the core technical judgment in GitHub Actions?
options: 每个 job 调度到用完即销毁的隔离环境（VM / microVM / 容器），并按账号限并发配额
所有 job 直接在同一批长期运行的共享主机上执行，job 之间不重建环境，以省掉冷启动
把用户 CI 脚本直接内联在调度器进程里执行
用一个全局队列串行跑完所有账号提交的 job
why: CI 跑的是不可信用户代码，前一个 job 的残留文件、进程和密钥不能留给下一个，所以每个 job 要在用完即销毁的隔离环境里跑；宿主机可以复用，但执行环境不能。并发配额防止单个账号占满 runner 池。代价是环境创建开销，常用预热池（warm pool）把它挪出关键路径。
why_en: CI runs untrusted user code, so leftover files, processes, and secrets from one job must never reach the next; each job runs in a single-use isolated environment that is destroyed afterward — hosts may be reused, execution environments may not. Per-account concurrency quotas stop any account from hogging the runner pool. The cost is environment setup, usually hidden behind a warm pool.
options_en: Schedule each job onto a single-use isolated environment (VM / microVM / container) that is destroyed afterward, and cap concurrency per account.
Run all jobs directly on the same long-lived shared hosts without rebuilding the environment between jobs, to skip cold starts.
Inline the user's CI script directly inside the scheduler process and run it there.
Run all accounts' submitted jobs serially through one global queue.

termDefinitions.meaning: 实际执行 CI job 的机器或进程（VM 或容器）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A runner is the machine or process (a VM or container) that actually executes a CI job.

termDefinitions.meaning: 资源受限、与主机及其他 job 隔离的执行环境。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sandbox is a resource-limited execution environment isolated from the host and from other jobs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 持续集成：每次代码变更自动构建和测试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Continuous Integration (CI) automatically builds and tests the codebase on every change.

termDefinitions.meaning: 限制单个账号可同时占用的 runner 数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A concurrency quota caps how many runners a single account can occupy at once.

optionExplanations: 对：CI 跑不可信代码，用完即销毁的隔离环境防止 job 间互相污染，配额防占满。
错：job 之间不重建执行环境，前一个 job 的残留和密钥会泄漏给下一个（宿主机可复用，执行环境不行）。
错：把用户脚本内联进调度器进程，等于让不可信代码跑在核心组件里。
错：全局串行跑所有 job，吞吐塌掉，一个慢 job 阻塞所有人。
optionExplanations_en: Right: CI runs untrusted code, so single-use isolated environments stop jobs from poisoning each other, and quotas prevent pool starvation.
Wrong: without rebuilding the execution environment between jobs, a prior job's leftover state and secrets leak into the next one (hosts may be reused, execution environments may not).
Wrong: inlining user scripts into the scheduler process runs untrusted code inside a core component.
Wrong: running all jobs serially in one global queue collapses throughput — one slow job blocks everyone.
